topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students, introduces the lecture series, and outlines the core learning objectives regarding the causes and mechanisms of cancer.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises from an interplay of endogenous mutations, stochastic bad luck, and environmental exposures, as highlighted by global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Agents and Mechanisms of Tumor Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological, physical, and chemical agents that cause cancer alongside the molecular mechanisms—such as metabolic activation, DNA adduct formation, and tumor promotion—that drive malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the analytical, epidemiological, and experimental methods used to identify carcinogens and prove their mutagenic effects on cells.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Balance
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by discussing everyday risk-benefit choices concerning carcinogenic exposures and summarizing key takeaways.
